characters.name: Dick Gumshoe
characters.description1: Homicide detective from the local precinct who's always first on the scene at any murder investigation.

characters.name: Florence Niedler
characters.description1: A nurse who works at Hertz Hospital. Has a worrying tendency to offer unnecessary treatments to everyone she meets.

characters.name: Kay Faraday
characters.description1: A mysterious young woman brought to the High Prosecutors' Offices by Florence Niedler. She appears to have lost her memory, but...
characters.description2: A self-styled Great Thief and so-called "second Yatagarasu". She's currently suffering from memory loss.

characters.name: Hilda Hertz
characters.description1: The head of Hertz Hospital. Carried out the preliminary inspection of the victim in this case.

characters.name: Franziska von Karma
characters.description1: Daughter of my mentor, Manfred von Karma. She is a highly talented prosecutor, and is currently working with Interpol.

characters.name: Eustace Winner
characters.description1: The greatest prosecutor ever to prosecute... according to himself, anyway. In actual fact, his relationship with logic is tenuous at best.

characters.name: Verity Gavèlle
characters.description1: A district court judge and member of the Committee for Prosecutorial Excellence, who also acts as its mouthpiece.

characters.name: Rosie Ringer
characters.description1: The victim in this case. She was a defense attorney, and served on the Committee alongside Judge Gavèlle.

characters.name: Excelsius Winner
characters.description1: Former chief prosecutor, current Chairman of the Committee, and Eustace Winner's father. Has a tendency to burst into tears over nothing.

characters.name: Eddie Fender
characters.description1: Senior partner at Edgeworth and Co. He's trying to get me to become a defense attorney.

characters.name: Ema Skye
characters.description1: A high school student looking to become a forensic investigator, and the younger sister of my former boss.

characters.name: Lotta Hart
characters.description1: A freelance photojournalist who I've met in the past. Known for her ability to sniff out scoops and snap them with her trusty camera.

evidences.name: Prosecutor's Badge
evidences.description1: Proof of my profession. However, I prefer to keep it in my pocket.

evidences.name: Yatagarasu Pin
evidences.description1: The Yatagarasu pin that Kay always wears.

evidences.name: Jammin' Ninja Mask
evidences.description1: A mask modeled on the Jammin' Ninja's face. Made of cheap plastic.

evidences.name: Letter
evidences.description1: A letter Kay was carrying. It is addressed to her.

evidences.name: Promise Notebook
evidences.description1: A book of promises Kay made to her father when she was a little girl. What was it doing in the Committee chamber?

evidences.name: Ticket Stub
evidences.description1: Stub from a ticket granting entry to the viewing platform on top of the Bigg Building.

evidences.name: Magenta Flower
evidences.description1: A magenta flower made of fabric that is usually worn on the chest as a decoration. Also known as a corsage.
evidences.description2: A magenta flower made of fabric that is usually worn on the chest as a decoration. Torn from the victim's clothes.

evidences.name: Bigg Building Pamphlet
evidences.description1: Contains a cross-section of the building and a plan of the viewing platform.

evidences.name: Kay's Recollections
evidences.description1: Kay remembers a person coming from beyond the concession stand and pushing her off of the building.

evidences.name: Candelabrum
evidences.description1: A three-armed candle holder that may have been the murder weapon, judging by the wounds to the the victim's chest.
evidences.description2: A three-armed candle holder found by the victim's body. Made to look like the murder weapon.

evidences.name: Keycard
evidences.description1: A keycard that grants entry to the Committee chamber. Found in the victim's hand.

evidences.name: Autopsy Report
evidences.description1: Initial findings of Dr. Hilda Hertz. Cause of death: Stab wounds to chest. Head injury sustained post mortem.
evidences.description2: Death occurred as a result of a heavy blow to the head with a circular object. Chest wounds inflicted post-mortem.

evidences.name: Keycard Record
evidences.description1: Record of keycards used to enter the Committee chamber.

evidences.name: Victim's Letter
evidences.description1: A letter that appears to have been written to the victim by Kay.

evidences.name: Broken Plushie
evidences.description1: The stuffed animal we originally found in the Zheng Fa presidential plane. Missing its left horn.
evidences.description2: Fitted with a recording device that captured part of a conversation. Based on the conversation, one of the people recorded was identified by having a prominent burn.

evidences.name: Masks
evidences.description1: A selection of various masks was kept on a rack. Each participant in the auction wore one.

evidences.name: Ringleader's Appearance
evidences.description1: Ringleader wore a white jacket, white gloves, a magenta flower, and a mask. Age and gender could not be discerned.
evidences.description2: Ringleader wore a white jacket, white gloves, a magenta flower, and a mask. Also had a tattoo on the part of their face the mask didn't cover.

evidences.name: Ms. Hart's Picture
evidences.description1: A photograph of the mysterious figure in the red raincoat. Click here for details. [caption] The figure's left hand is stained with blood. The figure is in the storeroom, walking towards a ladder that goes upwards. [info] The assult of Ms. Crane took place just before this photo was taken.

evidences.name: Ms. Hart's Statement
evidences.description1:
Ms. Hart's observations about what happened during the mysterious auction. [info] Illicit auction held in Bigg Building. Items on sale were mainly items of police evidence related to homicide cases.
Eleven attendees altogether. All were wearing masks.
Auction continued even after Ringer's murder, but the sound of the auctioneer's hammer could no longer be heard.

evidences.name: Elevator Blood
evidences.description1: Blood was detected on the secret elevator. It looks like it dripped through to the floor below.

evidences.name: Clothes Box
evidences.description1: Box in which the killer hid the body. Traces of blood were detected inside.

evidences.name: Committee Chamber Blood
evidences.description1: Blood found in the Committee chamber. Was it placed there to hide the existence of the storeroom?

evidences.name: Red Raincoat
evidences.description1: Worn by the victim, whose fingerprints and blood were found on the hood.

evidences.name: Nurse Niedler's Statement
evidences.description1: Niedler's description of how she swapped places with Rosie Ringer.

evidences.name: IS-7 Incident Case File
evidences.description1: Details of a murder case from eighteen years ago.

testimonies.testimony: The victim used her keycard and entered this room with the culprit.
Then, the culprit stabbed the victim in the chest with the candelabra, killing her.
Shouldn't the letter make it obvious who the culprit is?
Of course, the crime scene was right here in this room: the P.I.C. meeting room.
The proof is the bloodstain we found here in the meeting room! That settles it, Miles Edgeworth.

source.evidence_span: Blood was detected on the secret elevator. It looks like it dripped through to the floor below.
testimony_span: the crime scene was right here in this room: the P.I.C. meeting room.

context_span:
Lotta:
It was a black market auction, after all. They followed a fairly detailed procedure. First, the participants entered the storeroom from the viewin' platform one at a time. When they got in, they each took one of those masks on the wall over there... Funny thing 'bout those masks... They're all equipped with voice changers. Itty bitty ones. That way they wouldn't be recognized. They wanted to protect their... "an anemone"?
Ema:
You mean... their "anonymity"?
Lotta:
Yeah, that's it! Their "anomnintany"!
Edgeworth:
(Why not just say "identity" and make things easier for all of us...?)
Lotta:
After puttin' on the mask, they'd go down the lift, and the next feller would come right in. On the way back, it was the exact same thing, but in reverse. They'd come up one by one, return the mask, and head up outta the storeroom.

Ema:
Well then, let's head on down!
Ray:
Oh, have we decided on our next destination? Heeeey, Kay!
Kay:
Y-Yes, Mr. Shields!
Ray:
We wouldn't want you to get lost, so make sure you stay real close to Uncle Ray, kay?
Kay:
Right! I'll follow you closely, Mr. Shields.
Edgeworth:
(These two... Since when did they get along like that?)
Investigation Complete
April 5, 7:43 PMGrand TowerP.I.C. Meeting Room

turns.summarizedContext: Prosecutor Franziska explains that the crime scene is the P.I.C. meeting room on the 50th floor. One floor above, reachable by a hidden elevator, is the storeroom.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims the blood found in the meeting room proves the crime happened there.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests blood dripped from the elevator to the floor below.
Fact 3: The context suggests the floor below the elevator is the meeting room.
Prop 1: If blood from a location comes from another location, the blood cannot be used to prove the first location is the crime scene.

testimonies.testimony: Ms. Crane went to the black market auction as a customer.
The red raincoat was one of the items up for auction...
We believe that she left her seat after winning the bid for it.
The only exit from the storeroom is the hatch that leads to the viewing platform.
Ms. Crane went out to the viewing platform, where she was attacked by Kay Faraday.

The assult of Ms. Crane took place just before this photo was taken.

testimonies.testimony: That was how she met her end. And that concludes my summary of the case.

turns.summarizedContext: Prosecutor Gravelle is summarizing the case.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims Ms. Gravelle was assulted on the viewing platform.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests Ms. Gravelle was assulted just before the photo was taken.
Fact 3: The evidence also suggests the assailent was in the storeroon when the photo was taken.
Prop 1: If an assailent is in a location just before they assult someone, the assault happens in the same place.
Prop 2: If an assault happens in the storeroom, it does not happen in the viewing platform.
